summary: A scholar of Buddhist studies, Robert E. Buswell Jr. earned his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley (~1979–1985) and studied under Kusan Sunim. He served as a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles from circa 1986 through the 1990s.

Specializing in Japanology and Buddhist studies, Robert E. Morrell studied under doctoral supervisor Robert H. Brower and William H. McCullough. He held posts at Washington University in St. Louis, attested in 1985 and 2006.

Working in Indology, Robert E. Svoboda studied at the University of Oklahoma (~1970–1972) and mentored under Vimalananda (~1975–1983). In 2008, he was an adjunct member at the Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health.

A Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar, Robert F. Rhodes was a Ph.D. candidate at Harvard University. He served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1993–1997 and 2012–2014) and was a committee member for the Otani Society (attested 2000).

Working in religious and Buddhist studies, Robert Florida served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University. He later held an Emeritus Fellowship at the University of Victoria, attested between 2000 and 2005.
Specializing in Sinology and religious studies, Robert Ford Campany served as a professor at Indiana University from circa 1989 to 2004. Around 2010, he held an appointment at Vanderbilt University.

Working in Indology and other fields, Robert Gardner studied at Harvard University (~1944–1947). He later served as a professor at Harvard University from circa 1957 to 1997 and held a post at the University of Puget Sound.

A Japanology scholar, Robert H. Brower studied at Harvard (~1941–1944) and the University of Michigan (~1946–1952). He served at the University of Michigan (~1966–1988) as Chairman of the Department of Far Eastern Languages and Literatures.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology, Sharf earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1982–1991). He taught at McMaster (~1989–1995), Michigan (~1995–2003), and became D. H. Chen Distinguished Professor at UC Berkeley (~2004).

Specializing in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Robert J. Miller served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1953 to 1989. He was also a professor at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

A Buddhist studies scholar, Robert Kritzer earned his Ph.D. from the University of California, Berkeley by 1995 under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He served as an associate professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University, attested between 1999 and 2017.

Working in Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Robert L. Brown served as a professor at UCLA (~1986–2014) and as a curator in South and Southeast Asian art at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1980–2014).

A scholar of Indology and linguistics, Robert Lenz studied at Tartu Governorate Gymnasium and the Imperial University of Dorpat (1825–1828). He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University from circa 1835 to 1836.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, Robert M. Gimello earned his PhD at Columbia (~1968–1976). He headed Oriental Studies at the University of Arizona (~1981–2006) and served as a professor at Harvard University (attested 2004–2007).

Working in Indology and history/archaeology, Robert Maclagan studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1835–1837) and Addiscombe Military Seminary (~1837–1839). He served as Principal of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

Magliola earned his Ph.D. from Princeton (~1966–1970), working in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He was Distinguished Chair Professor at National Taiwan University (~1980–1990) and Professor of Philosophy and Religious Studies at Assumption University (~1990).

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Robert Mayer completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University under supervisors Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen. In 2002, he was an Oriental Studies faculty member at the University of Oxford.

Specializing in linguistics and Indology, Robert Needham Cust was educated at Eton College (~1834–1840) and Haileybury and Imperial Service College (~1840–1842). He served in the Bengal Civil Service from circa 1843 to 1867.

An Indologist, Robert P. Goldman studied at Columbia (~1960–1964) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1965–1971), supervised by Shivaram Dattatray Joshi and T. S. Srinivasa Sastri. He held a post at UC Berkeley beginning around 1971.

An art historian and archaeologist, Robert S. Nelson studied at Rice (~1965–1969) and New York University (~1970–1978). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago (~1974–2005) and subsequently held a post at Yale (~2005–2021).
